summary.title: MicroRNA-196a is regulated by ER and is a prognostic biomarker in ER+ Breast Cancer
summary.authors: Michael J G Milevskiy, Udai Gujral, Carolina Del Lama Marques, Andrew Stone, Korinne Northwood, Lez J Burke, Julia M W Gee, Kenneth Nephew, Susan Clark, Melissa A Brown, Mjg Milevskiy
summary.executive_summary: This study investigates the transcriptional regulation of MicroRNA-196a (MIR196A) and its role as a prognostic biomarker in breast cancer. The authors demonstrate that MIR196A expression is dynamically controlled by the oestrogen receptor (ERα) through complex long-range transcriptional interactions between promoter and enhancer elements. Specifically, the MIR196A2 locus, located within the HOXC cluster, is upregulated by oestradiol in MCF7 cells, a process mediated by ERα and its pioneer factor FOXA1 binding to putative promoters and distal enhancers, including the HOTAIR distal enhancer (HDE). Chromatin conformation capture (3C) and ChIA-PET analyses confirm physical interactions between these enhancers and the MIR196A2/HOXC10 promoter region. Clinically, MIR196A expression is significantly increased in models of hormone receptor-positive disease resistance, including tamoxifen-resistant and chemotherapeutic-resistant cell lines. In patient cohorts, high MIR196A expression correlates with poor survival in post-menopausal ER+ breast cancer, whereas it associates with better outcomes in pre-menopausal ER+ disease and triple-negative breast cancer. The study further reveals that DNA methylation patterns at the HOXC10/MIR196A2 promoters change in response to endocrine therapy resistance, suggesting that de-repression of these regulatory elements contributes to the development of therapeutic resistance. These findings establish MIR196A as a robust prognostic factor for advanced ER+ disease and provide insights into the epigenetic and transcriptional mechanisms driving breast cancer progression and resistance.

claims.description: MIR196A is transcriptionally regulated by oestrogen via ERα binding to specific promoter and enhancer elements.
High MIR196A expression is a prognostic biomarker for poor survival in post-menopausal ER+ breast cancer.
Therapeutic resistance leads to increased MIR196A expression and changes in DNA methylation.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study investigates the transcriptional regulation of MicroRNA-196a (MIR196A) and its role as a prognostic biomarker in breast cancer. The authors demonstrate that MIR196A expression is dynamically controlled by the oestrogen receptor (ERα) through complex long-range transcriptional interactions between promoter and enhancer elements. Specifically, the MIR196A2 locus, located within the HOXC cluster, is upregulated by oestradiol in MCF7 cells, a process mediated by ERα and its pioneer factor FOXA1 binding to putative promoters and distal enhancers, including the HOTAIR distal enhancer (HDE). Chromatin conformation capture (3C) and ChIA-PET analyses confirm physical interactions between these enhancers and the MIR196A2/HOXC10 promoter region. Clinically, MIR196A expression is significantly increased in models of hormone receptor-positive disease resistance, including tamoxifen-resistant and chemotherapeutic-resistant cell lines. In patient cohorts, high MIR196A expression correlates with poor survival in post-menopausal ER+ breast cancer, whereas it associates with better outcomes in pre-menopausal ER+ disease and triple-negative breast cancer. The study further reveals that DNA methylation patterns at the HOXC10/MIR196A2 promoters change in response to endocrine therapy resistance, suggesting that de-repression of these regulatory elements contributes to the development of therapeutic resistance. These findings establish MIR196A as a robust prognostic factor for advanced ER+ disease and provide insights into the epigenetic and transcriptional mechanisms driving breast cancer progression and resistance.

Research Context
MicroRNAs are short non-coding RNAs that post-transcriptionally regulate gene expression. MIR196A is transcribed from two loci, HOXC and HOXB. MIR196A has been implicated in a wide range of developmental and pathogenic processes. Genetic variants and altered expression of miR196a are associated with risk and progression of multiple cancers. Little is known about the regulation of the genes encoding this miRNA. The transcriptional regulation of miR-196a remains poorly understood. Promoters for miRNAs can be identified similarly to protein coding genes. Instances of miRNA regulation by enhancers have been described but are in their infancy.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aimed to characterise the expression landscape of MIR196A. The authors sought to determine if oestrogen regulates MIR196A2. It was hypothesized that MIR196A transcription may be controlled by the oestrogen receptor. The hypothesis was that MIR196A2 is controlled by long-range transcriptional regulation. The study explored potential roles of regulatory elements in breast cancer prognostication. The authors investigated the effects of menopause on the stratification of survival. The study examined whether therapeutic resistance leads to increases in MIR196A expression.

Methodological Details
MCF7 cells and endocrine resistance sub-lines were obtained from AstraZeneca. Cell lines were cultured for less than 6 months after authentication. Authentication was performed by short-tandem repeat (STR) profiling. PCR products were ligated into Invitrogen's pCR-Blunt plasmid. Enhancers and promoters were cloned into the luciferase reporter plasmid pGL3-Basic. MCF7 cells were transfected with 500 ng of modified pGL3 reporter constructs. Transfection included 20 ng of pRL-TK and 0.5μL of Lipofectamine 3000. Luciferase readings were measured using a DTX-880 luminometer. RNA was extracted using Life Technologies TRIzol reagent. RNA for miRNA analysis was reverse transcribed using the miScript RT II kit. Expression data for miRNAs was normalised to the snoRNA RNU6b. qRT-PCRs were performed on a Corbet Rotorgene-6000. RNA-Seq on MCF7 cells following oestradiol treatment was performed as described previously. RNA-Seq from Adriamycin and paclitaxel resistant cells was sourced from GSE68815. MCF7 ChIP-Seq data was sourced from GSE14664. GRO-Seq data was sourced from GSE27463. ChIA-PET data was sourced from GSE39495. Breast tumour ERα ChIP-Seq data was sourced from GSE32222. ChIP-Seq data was mapped with Bowtie and peaks called by MACS. DNA methylation of breast tumours was sourced from The Cancer Genome Atlas. METABRIC expression and clinical information were sourced from EGAS00000083. Clustering was performed using the Multiple Experiment Viewer (MeV). Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazard regression analyses were performed. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was done using GraphPad Prism. Optimal cutoffs were determined using receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curves. Chromosome conformation capture (3C) was adapted from Vakoc 2005. Cells were fixed with 1% formaldehyde for 3C. Libraries were generated using HindIII digestion.

Procedures And Architectures
Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP-Seq) for RNA polymerase II was used. Global-run-on sequencing (GRO-Seq) was used to measure nascent RNA. ChIA-PET was used to identify genome-wide chromatin interactions. Chromosome conformation capture (3C) digestion was performed on the HOXC locus. 3C-qPCR demonstrated that enhancer elements physically interact with promoters. Cloning of fragments into luciferase reporters demonstrated transcriptional augmentation. DNA methylation analysis was performed on MCF10A, MCF7, and HMEC cells. Hierarchical clustering of breast tumour RNA-Seq data was performed. Survival analysis stratified ER+ tumours by MIR196A expression. The study utilized expression data from the METABRIC cohort.

Key Results
MIR196A expression highly correlates to HOXC genes, particularly HOXC10. MIR196A expression is mostly within basal stem-cell derived cells. RNA production in the MIR196A2 region peaks at 40 mins following E2 addition. MIR196A2 is transcriptionally regulated by oestrogen. ERα and FOXA1 bind to putative promoters 1 and 3. PP1 is the most active promoter in MCF7 cells. Two major sites of interaction with MIR196A2 promoters were identified. One interacting partner is the HOTAIR distal enhancer (HDE). The other is a novel interacting partner (MIR196A2-Enhancer, mE). HDE appears to be the most active enhancer in MCF7 cells. The CpG island is mostly methylated in MCF10A and MCF7 cells. The CpG island is unmethylated in human mammary epithelial cells. MIR196A is significantly over-expressed in breast tumours compared to normal tissue. Over-expression is associated with an increase in tumour stage. High MIR196A expression is associated with poor survival in ER+ breast cancer. High expression associates with better outcome in triple-negative breast cancer. Women with low MIR196A expression had >95% survival at 10 years. Most women in the high expression group died within 17 years. 61% of high expression group died at 10 years. In premenopausal women, high MIR196A expression is associated with good outcome. In post-menopausal women, high MIR196A expression is associated with poor outcome. MIR196A expression is significantly increased in tamoxifen resistant MCF7 cells. MIR196A is almost depleted in fulvestrant resistance. MIR196A expression increases in resistant cell lines compared to sensitive lines. An increase in ERα occupancy is seen at enhancer and promoter regions.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
MIR196A displays complex and dynamic expression patterns. Expression is controlled by long range transcriptional regulation. The regulation involves ERα bound promoter and enhancer elements. Changes in regulation are associated with breast cancer progression. The pathway to resistance involves de-repression of promoter and enhancer elements. HOX genes may help tumour cells sustain a stem-cell like state. There is a change in regulation through and following menopause. MIR196A is a possible biomarker for progression to resistance.

Contradictions And Limitations
The association between MIR196A and HOXC genes is not significant in normal tissues. It is currently unclear how dual-encoded miRs are regulated. The effects of menopause on the human breast are largely unknown. PP3 is not able to increase luciferase expression in reporter assays. The study relies on cell line models which may not fully represent patient heterogeneity.

Claims
MIR196A is transcriptionally regulated by oestrogen via ERα binding to specific promoter and enhancer elements. ChIP-Seq shows polymerase binding is dependent on oestrogen. GRO-Seq indicates dramatic increase in RNA production after E2. ERα and FOXA1 bind to putative promoters 1 and 3. 3C-qPCR demonstrates physical interaction between enhancers and promoters. PP3 does not increase luciferase expression in reporter assays. 
High MIR196A expression is a prognostic biomarker for poor survival in post-menopausal ER+ breast cancer. High expression associates with poor survival in ER+ disease. 61% of high expression group died at 10 years. High expression is associated with poor outcome in post-menopausal women. High expression associates with good outcome in premenopausal women. High expression associates with better outcome in TNBC. MIR196A can be used for stratification of therapeutically resistant breast cancer.
Therapeutic resistance leads to increased MIR196A expression and changes in DNA methylation. MIR196A is significantly increased in tamoxifen resistant cells. Expression patterns match changes in DNA methylation. ERα occupancy increases in non-responders and metastases. MIR196A is almost depleted in fulvestrant resistance. De-repression of regulatory elements contributes to resistance.

Data And Code Availability
Accession codes for publically available data were provided. Data was sourced from ENCODE, TCGA, and GEO.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Validation was performed using qRT-PCR and RNA-Seq. 3C-qPCR was used to validate chromatin interactions. Luciferase reporter assays were used to test promoter/enhancer activity.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows ChIP-Seq, GRO-Seq, and qRT-PCR data for E2 regulation. Figure 2 shows ChIA-PET and 3C data for chromatin interactions. Figure 3 shows clustering of MIR196A expression in breast tumours. Figure 4 shows METABRIC expression and survival analysis. Figure 5 shows survival stratification and resistance models. Table 1 shows multivariate analysis for premenopausal women.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the elucidation of ERα-mediated long-range transcriptional regulation of MIR196A. 2. The strongest evidence is the correlation of high MIR196A expression with poor survival in post-menopausal ER+ patients. 3. The future path is to uncover the purpose of increased MIR196A expression in resistance.
